name: Rosewood Cape Kidnappers
positioning: Country lodge on a 6,000-acre working sheep and beef farm in Hawke's Bay, New Zealand, with a clifftop golf course and a gannet colony
best_for: Golfers who want a clifftop course with sea views
Wildlife and bird lovers interested in gannets, kaka and a guests-only conservation sanctuary
Groups or families wanting a four-bedroom villa for up to 8 guests

facts.text: Rosewood Cape Kidnappers is in Hawke's Bay, New Zealand.
The golf course was designed by Tom Doak.
Vegetables, fruits and herbs harvested from the property's own garden shape the seasonal cuisine.
The Dining Room's menu highlights local seasonal produce and changes daily.
Guests can also dine at the golf course clubhouse, which has a more casual menu.
Rooms are minimalist country-house chic, with lofted ceilings, timber trusses, off-white shiplap and barn doors.
Rooms have deep soaking tubs in front of picture windows overlooking the sea.
Grand Ridge Junior Suites sit on a skyline ridge with views over the farm and the Pacific Ocean.
Cape Sanctuary night tours introduce guests to New Zealand's nocturnal wildlife.
Complimentary activities change day to day and include flower-arranging classes, foraging workshops and farm tours.
Winery tours visit Hawke's Bay vineyards and wineries, and a Can-Am tour explores the property with an experienced local.
Spa treatment rooms are in a building just above the main lodge, with a terrace for tea after treatments.

highlights.text: The hotel describes its gannet colony as the largest, most accessible mainland colony of gannets in the world.
The property is a 6,000-acre working sheep and beef farm, where guests can join the farmer and his trained farm dogs for a shepherding experience.
Daytime and nighttime tours of Cape Sanctuary are offered exclusively to Cape Kidnappers guests.
The clifftop golf course, completed in 2004, sits in a ridge-and-valley landscape with sea views.
Nature's Dining Room is a gourmet picnic hamper of local food and wine to enjoy out in the landscape.

considerations.text: There is no kids club; families can instead watch sheepdogs at work, go hiking and encounter native birds.
Guests typically fly into the small regional airport at Napier, then drive along the coast and up into the hills.
WhataHotel notes the remote location requires significant travel planning.
